**STEP 1 - Scene:** A single slice-like portion of thin-crust pizza (cheese and tomato sauce, looks like a rectangular/square-cut piece with bread base) on a white square plate. Photographed from directly above.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white plate is square-ish, about 27 cm across its width (roughly dinner-plate size). Area ≈ 27 × 27 ≈ 730 cm² (treating it as a square; a round equivalent would be ~26 cm diameter, ~530 cm²). I'll use ~600 cm² as a middle estimate.

**STEP 3 - Items:** Pizza (cheese + tomato sauce on bread base). Only one food item is visible; no separate oil or dressing.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The pizza pieces cover roughly 12% of the plate (about 70 cm² of the ~600 cm² area), the rest is empty plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pizza pieces are thin, around 1.5–2 cm thick including cheese. 70 cm² × 1.8 cm ≈ 126 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Pizza is dense, bread/cheese-like, so bulk density ~0.9 g/ml. 126 ml × 0.9 ≈ 113 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cheese pizza is roughly 260–270 kcal per 100 g. 113 g × 2.65 ≈ 300 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Roughly 110 g and about 300 kcal fits about two medium slices-worth of thin cheese pizza visible on a plate. Plausible for the visible amount.
